scope.description: One real in-process cluster shape (three OmniPaxos actors over an in-memory transport, majority quorum, batch_size 1, node 1 forced into the leader role), run three times with different admissions, each case emitting its result under its own event name. Mode A (control): no partition, so entry 11 appended through the origin is replicated and decided normally. Modes B and C: node 1's links to both followers are cut in both directions, node 1 - still the leader in the accept phase - takes entry 11 (so it can only be accepted locally and assigned an index), the two followers elect node 3, which decides entry 22 at the same first index, and node 1 is then reconnected so the new leader re-synchronizes it. B and C differ only in the actor tick period (2 ms vs 80 ms), which controls whether a drain_notifiers pass can run between the origin's promise change and its decided-index advance.
assumptions: Message loss/partition is a permitted fault for this protocol; the core tolerates lost messages via its resend path, and the harness drops whole messages inside the transport without adding backpressure.
Each node is a real OmniPaxos instance with MemoryStorage, batch_size 1 and a majority quorum, driven only through the public actor handle; no target logic is modified.

Node 1 carries leader_priority 1 so the pre-partition leader is stable; a higher priority only breaks ties at equal ballot number, and in modes B/C the followers reach a strictly higher ballot number through the election-timeout takeover path.

drain_notifiers runs only from the tick branch, so the resolution instant is quantised by tick_period; the gap between the origin's Prepare handling and the AcceptSync that follows it is one round trip (about 2-4 ms here).
excluded: Any claim about entries other than the two submitted values (11 by the origin, 22 by the new leader).
Any claim about transports, runtimes or timings other than the in-process in-memory transport used here.
Durable/crash recovery: the origin is re-synchronized in-process, it is not restarted, so no storage-persistence claim follows from these cases.

basis.prefix: Per case: build three OmniPaxos instances (pids 1..3, configuration_id 1, nodes [1,2,3], MemoryStorage, batch_size 1, election_tick_timeout 3, node 1 leader_priority 1) and spawn each as an actor through spawn_actor with a tokio-backed AsyncRuntime adapter (tick_period per case, egress_period 1 ms). Wire every node's outgoing_messages() receiver into a task that consults a per-direction block set and, unless the link is blocked, delivers the message with peer.handle_incoming(). Admission: call handles[1].try_become_leader() until all three nodes report current_leader() == (1, true) and still do so after four election timeouts; emit the admission event carrying mode, cluster setup, origin 1, submitted_value 11 and the tick period. Mode A: await handles[1].append_notify(TestEntry(11)) and then read the origin's decided suffix, emitting the result as `notify_resolution_a`. Modes B/C: block (1,2) and (1,3) both ways, spawn handles[1].append_notify(TestEntry(11)) as a task, sleep one tick period, wait until nodes 2 and 3 both report a leader other than 1 with accepted=true, await handles[new_leader].append_notify(TestEntry(22)), then unblock both links and await the origin's future, emitting the result as `notify_resolution_b` or `notify_resolution_c` respectively. Every result event carries the resolved variant (ok / superseded / timeout / ...), the assigned index, the decided entry at that index and, only when that index was actually observed in the decided log, whether it equals the submitted value.
basis.responsibility: The decisive inputs are produced by the target itself: the actor assigns the caller's entry an index from its own local accept as leader, records the assignment as (index, ballot) with no entry identity, and drain_notifiers derives the resolution from the local decided index alone, evaluating the Ok arm before the ballot-change arm. The caller supplies only the entry value.

comparisons.description: Control: without a partition the success resolution names an index whose decided entry is the caller's entry.
Same lost-entry setup with a 2 ms tick: the documented heuristic resolution is the one delivered.

Same lost-entry setup with an 80 ms tick: if the resolution is Ok, the returned index must hold the caller's entry. A false value is the violating witness; if mode C resolves anything else, the antecedent does not hold and the assertion is not applicable.
